top_story.headline: Four FEC letters in two days press Denton County Republican Victory Fund on non-federal transfers, billboards and payroll
top_story.dek: The Texas party committee's April, June, July and September monthly reports all drew requests for additional information.
paragraphs: The FEC sent four requests for additional information to Denton County Republican Victory Fund on October 28 and 29. All are addressed to its treasurer, Christina S. Bradley. The letters cover the committee's April, June, July and September monthly reports. Three of them reference amended reports the committee filed on 09/08. Responses are due 12/02 and 12/03. The letters are requests for clarification, not findings.

The April letter says the committee's combined reports show $54,517.44 in transfers from its non-federal account for allocated activity, but only $31,285.06 as the non-federal share. It also asks about transfers tied to the 'Lincoln Reagan Dinner 2026 (01/10/2026)' that appear to exceed the allocation ratio. The FEC recommends the committee transfer any excess back to the non-federal account. Transfers for allocated activity must fall within 70 days of the vendor payment.

The July letter asks about a 'Billboard political advertising' payment allocated between federal and non-federal funds. The FEC says public communications that refer to a clearly identified candidate cannot be allocated and must use federal funds only. It also asks about payroll items allocated as non-federal ('Employer taxes,' 'Fundraising assistant,' 'Online & Social Media Labor,' 'Party payroll taxes,' 'Poll worker payroll'). The June letter raises the same payroll question for 'Party Payroll,' 'Party Payroll Taxes' and 'Party Wages.' The September letter says the report's beginning cash balance does not match the August ending balance and that Column B year-to-date totals appear incorrect.

sections.headline: Three sitting House members answer FEC questions; a fourth files a Form 1
paragraphs: Four filings carry sitting-lawmaker tags. Three are responses to earlier FEC letters about refunds and uncashed checks, and one is a Statement of Organization. Rep. Ralph Norman (R-SC) says he will give $700 in uncashed checks to charity.

items: Rep. Ralph Norman (R-SC) says his committee will disgorge $700 in uncashed checks to a charity. Ralph Norman for Congress says the checks relate to an intended refund to Black & Associates, whose permissibility as a source it could not determine. It says its 'uncashed checks' receipts on the July Quarterly otherwise produced no prohibited contributions. The gift will appear on the year-end report. Responding to an RFAI received 09/24 with a 10/29 due date. (Form 99)

Rep. Mike Bost (R-IL) tells the FEC an excessive contribution from National Pork Producers Council Pork PAC was refunded on 08/26. Mike Bost for Congress Committee says the refund was reported on its October Quarterly filed 10/15. It adds that contributions designated to the 2026 primary but received after the primary were refunded as well. Responding to an RFAI on the July Quarterly. (Form 99)

Rep. Sylvia R. Garcia (D-TX) asks the FEC to accept a Form 1 so she can reset a password. Sylvia Garcia for Congress says it no longer has access to the email on file. The cover letter and the Form 1 text cite committee ID C00657304, while the filing is indexed under C00660555. The Form 1 lists a Houston address and a designated agent in Washington. (Form 99)

Rep. Trent Kelly (R-MS) files a Form 1 Statement of Organization for Kelly for Congress. The scan is badly garbled. Legible parts show a principal campaign committee for a House candidate, a treasurer who appears to be Fred Page and a Huntington National Bank account. A line 6 entry appears to name a connected organization or sponsor, but the text is too distorted to read reliably. (Form 99)

sections.headline: Fifteen RFAIs, led by party-committee allocation questions and late independent expenditure reports
paragraphs: All 15 letters went to PACs or party committees. No candidate committees are in this batch. The largest cluster is the four Denton County Republican Victory Fund letters covered above. Six letters concern 24-Hour or 48-Hour independent expenditure reports. The rest are a mix of template issues, including a missing purpose, an undisclosed depository and an unsigned report.

items: FEC asks Planned Parenthood Action Fund of the Pacific Southwest PAC to supply the office sought for candidates in its 24-Hour independent expenditure report. The report was received 10/17. The same treasurer, Kurt Gering, received a second letter for the amended report. Response due 12/03. (RFAI)
FEC repeats the missing office-sought request to Planned Parenthood Action Fund of the Pacific Southwest PAC for its amended 24-Hour report. The amended report was received 10/19. (RFAI)
FEC asks Progressive Promise to supply the state missing from its 24-Hour independent expenditure report. The report was received 10/20, and the treasurer is Jason Hinton. Response due 12/03. (RFAI)

FEC asks Abundant Future whether it failed to file timely 24-Hour reports on last-minute independent expenditures. The question comes from Schedule E of its amended July Quarterly received 09/14. The treasurer is Nicholas Sanders. Response due 12/03. (RFAI)

FEC sends Real Fight NYC what appears to be the same late-reporting question put to Abundant Future. Its letter on the July Quarterly (04/01 to 06/30) repeats the standard text printed in Abundant Future's letter. The treasurer is Jonathan Robert Ronayne. (RFAI)

FEC asks Workers Vote whether it failed to file timely 48-Hour reports for independent expenditures of $10,000 or more. The letter cites Schedule E of its September Monthly report. The treasurer is Zaina Tannu. Response due 12/03. (RFAI)

FEC asks Denton County Republican Victory Fund, a party committee, about April transfers of $54,517.44 from its non-federal account against a $31,285.06 non-federal share. The letter also asks about 'Lincoln Reagan Dinner 2026 (01/10/2026)' transfers that appear to exceed the allocation ratio. It concerns the amended April Monthly received 09/08. Response due 12/02. (RFAI)

FEC asks Denton County Republican Victory Fund why 'Billboard political advertising' and payroll items were allocated to non-federal funds. The payroll items include 'Poll worker payroll' and 'Online & Social Media Labor.' The letter concerns the amended July Monthly received 09/08. Response due 12/02. (RFAI)

FEC asks Denton County Republican Victory Fund whether 'Party Payroll,' 'Party Payroll Taxes' and 'Party Wages' were for employees who spent 25% or less of their time on federal election activity. If not, the letter says the non-federal reimbursement must be returned. It concerns the amended June Monthly received 09/08. Response due 12/03. (RFAI)

FEC tells Denton County Republican Victory Fund that its September Monthly opening cash does not match the August closing balance. The letter also says Column B year-to-date totals on lines 6(c), 11(a)(i), 11(a)(ii), 11(a)(iii), 11(d), 19 and 20 appear incorrect. Response due 12/02. (RFAI)

FEC asks United Postmasters and Managers of America Political Fund about $6,000 in Schedule B memo entries that match no itemized transaction. The letter also says some activity sits on the wrong lines of the Detailed Summary Page. It concerns the October Monthly report, and the treasurer is Daniel Heins. (RFAI)

FEC says Black America's Political Action Committee left the purpose blank on itemized Line 21(b) disbursements. The letter concerns its October Quarterly, and the treasurer is Alvin Williams. Response due 12/03. (RFAI)

FEC asks Democratic Party of Virginia to disclose 'First Indiana Bank Of Indiana' as a depository. The bank paid interest reported on the September Monthly but is not on the committee's Statement of Organization. The treasurer is Abbi Easter. Response due 12/03. (RFAI)

FEC says HighPoint Global LLC Citizen Experience Fund's October Quarterly was not signed by an authorized treasurer or agent. The letter asks for an amendment with a proper signature. If a new treasurer has been appointed, it asks for an amended Statement of Organization. The listed treasurer is Chad Pryor. Response due 12/02. (RFAI)

FEC tells NYC-DSA Federal PAC it does not yet qualify for multicandidate status because it has not contributed to five federal candidates. This is a reply to its Form 1M, and the treasurer is Jeremy Cohan. Response due 12/03. (Filing)

sections.headline: Seventeen Form 99 submissions, mostly RFAI responses and credential or setup requests
paragraphs: Most of these are replies to earlier RFAIs. Several others are access or setup requests, including password resets and a test filing. One candidate forgives a personal loan and another asks to close out. One presidential-candidate submission is unintelligible and contains no compliance content.

items: Jay Vaingankar forgives the remaining $53,000 on a loan he made to his own committee. The notice was filed under the form type Loan Forgiveness for Jay Vaingankar for Congress, a Democratic open-seat House candidate in New Jersey. (Form 99)

Congressional Black Caucus PAC tells the FEC it is still auditing its books to find the cause of cash-on-hand errors and missing transactions. It says that as of 10/28 it amended its December 2025 Monthly and Year End 2025 reports. It is responding to an RFAI dated May 12 about an opening balance that did not match the prior report. (Form 99)

Gun Rights America tells the FEC its independent expenditures to ColorSpray Media and PXI Inc. were properly reported as estimates. It says they were disclosed on the 04/23 48-Hour Report in connection with candidates identified only as Massie and Gallrein. It says a 'Mudshare' expenditure was only anticipated and never disseminated, so no report was required. It is responding to an RFAI received 09/24 with a 10/29 due date. (Form 99)

Civic Renewal Fund Inc. tells the FEC it amended a 24-Hour independent expenditure notice to fix rounding errors in cumulative totals. The errors affected FL-22, KY-06, NM-02, SC-01 and WI-01. The notice was first filed 10/24 and amended 10/29. The committee says no individual expenditure amounts changed. The treasurer is Britney Gonzalez. (Form 99)

Colorado Turnout Project says all excessive contributions have been refunded. The refunds will appear on the Post-General Report. It also explains that Fighting for Colorado PAC is a Colorado state committee supporting Phil Weiser for governor. It is responding to an RFAI dated 09/24. (Form 99)

California Democratic Party says $12,750 in strategic consulting went to Yvette Martinez, who is not an employee. It also says its 401(k) payments covered employees who spent under 25% of their time on federal election activity, and it amended the August Monthly to say so. Treasurer Teddy Kapur also argues that 'campaign finance data imports' are not federal election activity. (Form 99)

Ohio Republican Party State Central & Executive Committee says employees keep daily work logs so anyone over the 25% federal-activity limit is not allocated. Treasurer Diane Cunningham Redden is responding to an RFAI dated 10/05 on the 2026 M8 amended report. (Form 99)

Washington State Republican Party says it amended its January Monthly to remove duplicate receipts already on the year-end report. It calls the duplication a clerical error. It also says payroll for employees under the 25% federal-activity threshold was allocated to administrative expenses. It is responding to an RFAI dated 09/23. (Form 99)

Banner Up notifies the FEC of a non-contribution account opened at Truist Bank on 10/26 with a $100 deposit. The nonconnected committee filed its Statement of Organization the same day. It cites the Carey v. FEC consent judgment, and the treasurer is Matei Diaconu. (Form 99)

America Now files a Form 1 Statement of Organization. It lists treasurer Scott M. Carr, a PNC bank account and a P.O. Box in Indianapolis. Line 6 contains the entry 'Carson, Andre,' with a different P.O. Box, but the relationship box is not legible. (Form 99)

TD PAC files a Form 1 Statement of Organization naming Leslie Compton as treasurer. The Chicago-based committee lists no connected organization and what appears to be an Amalgamated Bank account in New York. The scan is partly garbled. (Form 99)
Randy Miller for Congress asks the FEC to close out its account as soon as possible. The one-line note comes from a committee in Lone Jack, Missouri. (Form 99)
Carolina Federation asks the FEC to reset a password. Joe Patton says he has neither the key nor the original email address for the account. (Form 99)

Capitol Compliance Associates asks the FEC to change the contact email for MomsRising Together to momsrising@capcompliance.com. Compliance manager Chelsie Torrence says the client cannot get its filing credentials. (Form 99)
Independent by Choice / Independent by Necessity PAC says it is trying to submit a filing and asks for advice. The one-line message was received 10/28. (Form 99)
FECFile+ Test PAC submits a Form 99 that reads only 'Test'. It lists an FEC-area address on E Street NW. (Form 99)

Presidential candidate James Walter Legate Jr files a rambling submission. It mentions an NFL free-agent contract and a Bexar County docket number, 2025CI21896. It contains no recognizable campaign-finance content. (Form 99)

paragraphs: 440 new independent expenditures of $50K or more, $238,329,062 in all. Largest target: Jon Husted (oppose, $14,888,982). 1 shared-vendor overlap between a campaign and a supporting super PAC. 34 spender(s) registered in the last 180 days.

blocks.text: Independent expenditures of $50K+ reported since 10/27/2026 (24/48-hour notices plus regular reports), counting only items not shown in an earlier edition. A shared vendor is a coordination-risk flag, not proof: FEC rules allow common vendors behind a firewall. Generic platforms (ActBlue, Google, postal, banks, broadcasters) are excluded.

footer.known_gaps: The Schedule A fetch for voided and negative transactions failed with an HTTP 504 query timeout, so no voided or negative-amount rows were checked in this edition. Several Form 1 scans (Kelly for Congress, Sylvia Garcia for Congress, America Now, TD PAC) have garbled text layers.

apod.title: Haunting the Cepheus Flare
apod.caption: Spooky shapes seem to haunt this dusty expanse, drifting through the night in the royal constellation Cepheus. Of course, the shapes are cosmic dust clouds visible in dimly reflected starlight.
